title: All beings freed, none freed (section 3)
hookLine: lead all beings to nirvana, yet no being is led, because a bodhisattva has no idea of a self

cards: A volunteer at a food bank goes home after a long shift. Somebody asks, how many people did you help today? It's a fair question.
There's a clipboard. There's a number. And yet something about the question sits a little wrong, as if the people who came through the line were points on a scoreboard.
The Diamond Sutra's first answer to Subhuti goes right at that discomfort. Free every being, it says. And then: no being has been freed.

teach.b: First, the size of the vow. The Buddha tells Subhuti how one on the bodhisattva path should think.
All beings, of every kind: born from an egg, from a womb, from moisture, or appearing all at once; with form or without; with perception, without it, or neither.
All of them I must lead into nirvana, the kind that leaves nothing behind.
It echoes the first of the four great vows. Second, the cut. Here the diamond comes in: and yet, after leading beings beyond measure to nirvana, no being at all has been led.
That isn't a riddle tossed off for effect. It's the sutra's first real move. Third, the reason the text gives.
If a bodhisattva held the idea of a being, they couldn't be called a bodhisattva.

Nor if they held the idea of a self, or a living thing, or a person. The helper who keeps a tally of the helped has already turned people into things that can be counted, and turned themselves into the one who counts.
Fourth, what it isn't saying. It isn't saying don't help. The vow to free all beings stands, at full size.
It's saying help without building a self out of the helping.
Some readers hear freedom for the helper too: no ledger to keep, no score to defend, no hero in the story.
And this week points the same way: merit given away, a book honored, two views held in good faith, a wide vehicle looked back on, a morning done fully, a question asked well.

how: Section 3 of the Diamond Sutra is chanted and studied in Mahayana communities as a teaching on the bodhisattva vow: to free all beings while holding no idea of a self, a being, a living thing or a person.

o: only beings born as humans can be led to freedom
lead every being to freedom, yet count no being as freed
everyone is free already, so no one needs any help

games.q: no one to count: tap the pairs.
p: no idea of a self or a being

s: the Diamond Sutra says don't bother helping, since no one is freed
the vow to free all beings stands at full size; it's the tally that goes.
the sutra's list of beings includes those born from eggs and from moisture
every kind of being, with form or without, is in the vow.
a bodhisattva who holds the idea of a self can't be called a bodhisattva
that's the reason the text gives for 'no being has been led'.

games.q: you've led beings beyond measure to nirvana. what does the Diamond Sutra say has happened?
o: a great store of merit has been earned
no being at all has been led
games.why: no being has been led, because a bodhisattva holds no idea of a being or a self. the help is real; the ledger isn't.

practice: Bring to mind one good thing you did for someone recently, and notice if a little voice says, that was good of me. Don't fight it; watch it, the way you'd watch a cloud cross a window.
Then let the picture change: not me helping them, just help happening, no helper, no helped, no number.

wordCard.voice: All beings freed. Lead every being to nirvana, the Diamond Sutra says, and yet no being is led, because a bodhisattva holds no idea of a self or a being. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the idea of a being, which the Diamond Sutra says a bodhisattva does not hold.

carryVoice: Your line: no one to count. Help every being, and keep no tally. A week, done.
